description: Backend: create an idempotent email_log table (migration) and stop the shared-inbox BCC flood at its source in the two edge functions, while writing an authoritative sent-email record from inside each edge function. This kills the process-reminders flood path (1000 followups) and the send-client-email force-BCC, and replaces the inbox copy with a real in-CRM record. Logging happens in ONE place (the edge functions) to avoid double-counting. Independent of FEAT-002 for the migration/edge-fn changes, but FEAT-002's UI reads the table this creates.
steps: Confirm baseline before editing: run `npx tsc --noEmit` (expect exit 0) and `git status` on branch. If not already on it, create feature branch `feat/stop-inbox-bcc-flood-email-log` off main.

Create setup/ADD_EMAIL_LOG.sql: an IDEMPOTENT migration (use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, and DROP POLICY IF EXISTS before CREATE POLICY; guard enum/column adds). Table public.email_log with columns: id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(); to_email TEXT NOT NULL; subject TEXT; sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(); status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sent' (CHECK in ('sent','failed')); resend_message_id TEXT; lead_id UUID REFERENCES public.leads(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; booking_id UUID (nullable, no FK requirement if bookings table name uncertain — verify bookings table name in setup SQL first; add FK only if the table exists, else keep as plain UUID with a comment); source TEXT (e.g. 'send-client-email','process-reminders'); created_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL; error TEXT; created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). Add indexes on (lead_id, sent_at DESC) and (booking_id, sent_at DESC). ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

Add RLS policies on email_log mirroring the lead_activities/leads read pattern from setup/COMBINED_DATABASE_SETUP.sql: SELECT for authenticated where is_admin(auth.uid()) OR created_by = auth.uid() OR (lead_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM public.leads l WHERE l.id = lead_id AND (l.assigned_to = auth.uid() OR l.created_by = auth.uid() OR has_role documentation/accounts/renewals/bd))). INSERT policy WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) so authenticated clients could insert, but note the service role (edge functions) bypasses RLS anyway. Do NOT add UPDATE/DELETE policies (append-only log; admins can manage via service role).

Edit supabase/functions/send-client-email/index.ts: (a) Remove the forced shared-inbox BCC. Keep honoring a caller-passed `bcc` only (drop the `...toEmailList(BCC_EMAIL)` merge and the BCC_EMAIL env read, OR keep the env read but do NOT append it by default — end result MUST be: no shared-inbox copy unless a caller explicitly passes bcc). Prefer removing the BCC_EMAIL default-append entirely and deleting the now-unused const + its comment. (b) Accept optional `lead_id`, `booking_id`, `created_by` in the request JSON. (c) After a SUCCESSFUL send (res.ok, id parsed), create a service-role Supabase client (import createClient from esm.sh like process-reminders does; read SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY which are injected automatically) and insert one row into email_log { to_email: toList joined or first, subject, resend_message_id: id, lead_id: lead_id||null, booking_id: booking_id||null, source:'send-client-email', created_by: created_by||null, status:'sent' }. Wrap the log insert in try/catch so a logging failure NEVER breaks the send response. Log for EACH recipient OR store the joined recipient list as a single row — choose single row per invocation with to_email = toList.join(',') to keep counts = number of sends; document the choice in a comment.

Edit supabase/functions/process-reminders/index.ts: (a) Remove the forced BCC — delete `if (BCC_EMAIL) payload.bcc = [BCC_EMAIL];` and the BCC_EMAIL env const so reminders never BCC the shared inbox. (b) It already has a service-role `supabase` client and the reminder row (r) with lead-linkage — verify whether reminders has a lead_id column by checking setup SQL (setup/ADD_REMINDERS.sql / COMBINED). After each successful send (inside the try, right after sendEmail succeeds), insert one email_log row { to_email: r.to_email, subject: r.subject, resend_message_id: capture Resend id by having sendEmail return the parsed id, lead_id: r.lead_id (only if the column exists; else null), source:'process-reminders', status:'sent' }. Also insert a row with status:'failed' and error in the catch branch (optional but recommended for parity). Ensure the reminders.occurrences_sent update logic is UNCHANGED. Wrap log inserts in try/catch so logging never blocks the reminder pipeline.
Update the header-comment secret docs in BOTH edge functions to note CRM_BCC_EMAIL is no longer force-applied (or removed) and that sends are now recorded in email_log.

Evaluate CRM_MARKER: its only stated purpose is Gmail-filtering the BCC'd copies (per the code comments). Since the default BCC is removed, the marker no longer serves the shared-inbox filter. However removing it is a body change to client-facing emails. Decide conservatively: KEEP the CRM_MARKER (it is invisible and harmless, and a user who opts back into BCC via caller-passed bcc still benefits) but update its comment to reflect that BCC is now opt-in. Document this decision in findings. Do NOT remove it unless verified to have no other consumer (grep already shows only these two functions reference it).
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm 0 new errors (edge functions are Deno and not part of the vite tsc project, but the frontend must still typecheck).
acceptance_criteria: setup/ADD_EMAIL_LOG.sql exists, is idempotent (re-runnable without error), creates public.email_log with the specified columns, indexes, RLS enabled, and SELECT/INSERT policies mirroring lead_activities.

supabase/functions/send-client-email/index.ts no longer appends a shared-inbox BCC by default; it accepts optional lead_id/booking_id/created_by and inserts an email_log row on successful send via a service-role client, inside try/catch.
supabase/functions/process-reminders/index.ts no longer sets payload.bcc from CRM_BCC_EMAIL; it inserts an email_log row per successful reminder send; occurrences_sent update logic is unchanged.
A logging failure cannot break the email send (all log inserts are try/caught).
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no new errors.
verification: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm exit 0 / no new errors.
Grep the two edge functions to confirm no unconditional `payload.bcc = [BCC_EMAIL]` / forced BCC_EMAIL merge remains.
Read setup/ADD_EMAIL_LOG.sql and confirm CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guards make it re-runnable.
findings: DONE. Created setup/ADD_EMAIL_LOG.sql (idempotent: CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, DROP POLICY IF EXISTS before CREATE). Verified in setup/COMBINED_DATABASE_SETUP.sql that BOTH public.leads and public.bookings tables exist, so booking_id got a real FK (bookings(id) ON DELETE SET NULL) rather than a plain UUID. RLS SELECT policy mirrors lead_activities/leads (is_admin OR created_by OR lead visible via assigned_to/created_by/has_role documentation|accounts|renewals|bd); INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL). No UPDATE/DELETE policy (append-only). is_admin/has_role helpers confirmed present in COMBINED_DATABASE_SETUP.sql. Verified in setup/ADD_REMINDERS.sql that reminders HAS a lead_id column (uuid REFERENCES leads), so process-reminders logs r.lead_id. send-client-email: removed the BCC_EMAIL default-append and const; BCC is now strictly caller opt-in (payload.bcc only from the caller's `bcc` param). Added optional lead_id/booking_id/created_by to request JSON. Logs one email_log row per invocation (to_email = toList.join(',')) via a service-role createClient after a successful send, wrapped in try/catch. process-reminders: removed BCC_EMAIL const and `if (BCC_EMAIL) payload.bcc=[BCC_EMAIL]`; sendEmail now returns the parsed Resend id; logs an email_log row (source 'process-reminders', status 'sent') after each successful send and a status 'failed' row (with error) in the catch branch, both try/caught. occurrences_sent update logic UNCHANGED. CRM_MARKER DECISION: KEPT in both functions (invisible/harmless; still useful for callers who opt back into BCC), comments updated to note BCC is now opt-in/removed. Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 (baseline clean, no new errors); `bun run build` exit 0 (emits dist/server). Edge functions are Deno, not part of the vite tsc project. FEAT-002 (frontend BCC removal + UI) and FEAT-003 (docs) are separate.
